translations.idiomatic: Who could have imagined such boundless wickedness and perversity? From childhood onward, no small good that he did not violate, no great evil that he did not commit.

sentences.zh: 前後訓誘，常加隱蔽，險戾難移，日月滋甚。

translations.literal: Again and again he was admonished and guided, yet this was constantly concealed; vicious and recalcitrant, he could not be turned, and day by day it grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he was admonished and guided, yet this was constantly concealed from view. Vicious and unyielding, he could not be changed, and day by day he grew worse.

sentences.zh: 棄冠毀冕，長襲戎衣，犬馬是狎，鷹隼是愛，皁歷軒殿之中，韝緤宸扆之側。

translations.literal: He cast off cap and crown, constantly wore military garb, doted on dogs and horses and loved hawks and falcons; he trod inked shoes in the palace halls and carried hawk's gloves at the imperial screen's side.
translations.idiomatic: He cast off cap and crown and constantly wore military dress; he doted on dogs and horses and loved hawks and falcons. He walked in ink-black shoes through the palace halls and carried hawk's gloves beside the imperial screen.

sentences.zh: 至乃單騎遠郊，獨宿深野，手揮矛鋋，躬行刳斮，白刃為弄器，斬害為恒務。

translations.literal: He even rode alone to distant outskirts and slept alone in deep wilds, wielding spear and iron staff with his own hands, personally performing dismemberment; naked blades were his playthings, killing his constant occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He even rode alone to distant suburbs and slept alone in deep wilderness, wielding spear and iron-shafted blade with his own hands and personally performing dismemberment. Naked blades were his toys; killing was his daily work.

sentences.zh: 捨交戟之衞，委天畢之儀，趨步闤闠，酣歌壚肆，宵遊忘反，宴寢營舍，奪人子女，掠人財物，方筴所不書，振古所未聞。

translations.literal: He abandoned the crossed-halberd guard and cast off the ritual canopy; he hurried through market quarters and caroused in wine shops; night outings forgot return, feasts and sleep in barracks; he seized people's sons and daughters and plundered their goods — what the records do not record, what from antiquity's founding has never been heard.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the crossed-halberd guard and cast off the ritual canopy, hurried through market streets and caroused in taverns, went out at night and forgot to return, feasted and slept in barracks, seized people's sons and daughters, and plundered their goods — things the records do not record and that have never been heard since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 沈勃儒士，孫超功臣，幼文兄弟，並豫勳効，四人無罪，一朝同戮。

translations.literal: Shen Bo was a scholar, Sun Chao a meritorious minister, the Youwen brothers had shared in meritorious service — four men without crime, in one morning together executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bo was a scholar, Sun Chao a meritorious minister, and the Youwen brothers had all shared in meritorious service. Four innocent men were executed together in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 飛鏃鼓劍，孩稚無遺，屠裂肝腸，以為戲謔，投骸江流，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: He shot arrows and brandished swords — no child left alive; he butchered and tore livers and guts as sport and cast corpses into the river's current for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He shot arrows and brandished swords until no child was left alive; he butchered and tore out livers and guts for sport and cast corpses into the river for amusement.

sentences.zh: 又淫費無度，帑藏空竭，橫賦關河，專充別蓄，黔庶嗷嗷，厝生無所。

translations.literal: Moreover he spent lasciviously without limit until the treasury was exhausted; he levied harsh taxes across passes and rivers solely to fill private hoards; the common people cried out in distress with nowhere to place their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he spent without limit until the treasury was empty; he levied harsh taxes across the passes and rivers solely to fill private stores, and the common people cried out in distress with nowhere to turn for their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 吾與其所生每厲以義方，遂謀酖毒，將騁凶忿。

translations.literal: I and his birth mother each sternly urged him by the righteous way, whereupon he plotted poison to vent his vicious rage.
translations.idiomatic: His birth mother and I each sternly urged him in the way of righteousness, whereupon he plotted poison to vent his vicious rage.

sentences.zh: 沈憂假日，慮不終朝。

translations.literal: Deep worry borrowed days; I feared I would not see another morning.
translations.idiomatic: Deep sorrow borrowed me days; I feared I would not live to see another morning.

sentences.zh: 自昔辛、癸，爰及幽、厲，方之於此，未譬萬分。

translations.literal: From Xin and Gui of old down to You and Li of Zhou — compared with this, not one ten-thousandth can describe it.
translations.idiomatic: From Xin and Gui of old down to You and Li of Zhou — compared with this, not one part in ten thousand can describe it.

sentences.zh: 民怨既深，神怒已積，七廟阽危，四海褫氣。

translations.literal: Popular resentment had deepened, divine wrath had accumulated; the seven temples teetered in peril, the four seas lost their breath.
translations.idiomatic: The people's resentment had deepened and divine wrath had accumulated; the seven temples stood on the brink of peril, and the four seas lost their breath.

sentences.zh: 廢昏立明，前代令範，況迺滅義反道，天人所棄，釁深牧野，理絕桐宮。

translations.literal: Deposing the dim and enthroning the bright was a model of former ages; how much more when he extinguished righteousness and rebelled against the Way, abandoned by heaven and men — offense as deep as Muye, reason as ended as the Palace of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing the dim and enthroning the bright was the worthy precedent of former ages; how much more when he extinguished righteousness and rebelled against the Way, abandoned by heaven and men — an offense as deep as at Muye, a case as closed as the Palace of Tong.

sentences.zh: 故密令蕭領軍潛運明略，幽顯協規，普天同泰。

translations.literal: Therefore I secretly charged Commandant Xiao to work a bright design in secret; the hidden and the manifest joined in plan, all under heaven sharing peace.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I secretly charged Commandant Xiao to carry out a bright design in secret; the hidden and the manifest joined in counsel, and all under heaven would share in peace.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍安成王體自太宗，天挺淹叡，風神凝遠，德映在田。

translations.literal: The Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Ancheng, by person descended from Emperor Ming, heaven-endowed with deep wisdom, spirit and bearing gathered and far-reaching, virtue shining even in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Ancheng, by descent came from Emperor Ming; heaven had endowed him with deep wisdom, his spirit and bearing were concentrated and far-reaching, and his virtue shone even in the fields.

sentences.zh: 地隆親茂，皇曆攸歸，億兆係心，含生屬望。

translations.literal: Ground lofty, kin flourishing, the imperial succession destined to him; the hundred millions bound their hearts, all living beings turned their hopes.
translations.idiomatic: His position was lofty and his kin flourishing; the imperial succession was destined for him. The hundred millions bound their hearts to him, and all living beings turned their hopes to him.

sentences.zh: 宜光奉祖宗，臨享萬國。

translations.literal: He should brightly serve the ancestors and preside over the enjoyment of the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: He should brightly serve the ancestors and preside over the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 便依舊典，以時奉行。

translations.literal: Let the old regulations be followed and carried out in due season.
translations.idiomatic: Let the established regulations be followed and carried out in due season.

sentences.zh: 未亡人追往傷懷，永言感絕。

translations.literal: The one who survives grieves for what is past and is wounded at heart; forever speaking, I am cut off by feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I who survive grieve for what is past and am wounded at heart; speaking of it forever, I am cut off by sorrow.

sentences.zh: 太后又令曰：「昱窮凶極暴，自取灰滅，雖曰罪招，能無傷悼。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued another order: "Yu was wicked to the utmost and violent to the extreme; he brought ash and extinction on himself. Though it is said guilt summoned this, how could there be no grief?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager issued another order: "Yu was wicked to the utmost and violent to the extreme; he brought ruin on himself. Though it is said his guilt summoned this, how could there be no grief?

sentences.zh: 棄同品庶，顧所不忍。

translations.literal: Abandoning the way shared with commoners is what I cannot bear to contemplate.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the way we share with commoners is what I cannot bear to contemplate.

sentences.zh: 可特追封蒼梧郡王。

translations.literal: He may be specially posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be specially posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 」葬丹陽秣陵縣郊壇西。

translations.literal: " He was buried west of the suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He was buried west of the suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初昱在東宮，年五六歲時，始就書學，而惰業好嬉戲，主帥不能禁。

translations.literal: Early on, when Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six years of age he first undertook book learning, yet was idle in studies and fond of play; his tutors could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six years of age he first began formal study, yet he was idle in his lessons and fond of play, and his tutors could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 好緣漆帳竿，去地丈餘，如此者半食久，乃下。

translations.literal: He liked to climb lacquered curtain poles more than a zhang above the ground and would stay thus for half a meal's time before coming down.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to climb lacquered curtain poles more than a zhang above the ground and would remain there for half a meal before coming down.

sentences.zh: 年漸長，喜怒乖節，左右有失旨者，輒手加撲打。

translations.literal: As he gradually grew older, joy and anger lost proper measure; attendants who failed to please him he would strike with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older his joy and anger lost all proper measure; attendants who displeased him he would beat with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 徒跣蹲踞，以此為常。

translations.literal: Barefoot and squatting — this became his habit.
translations.idiomatic: Going barefoot and squatting became his constant habit.

sentences.zh: 主帥以白太宗，上輒敕昱所生，嚴加捶訓。

translations.literal: The tutors reported to Emperor Ming; the throne would order Yu's birth mother to beat and discipline him severely.
translations.idiomatic: The tutors reported to Emperor Ming, who would then order Yu's birth mother to beat and discipline him severely.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，內畏太后，外憚諸大臣，猶未得肆志。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, inwardly he feared the empress dowager and outwardly dreaded the various ministers — he had not yet been able to give free rein to his will.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne he still feared the empress dowager within and dreaded the ministers without, and had not yet been able to indulge his will fully.

sentences.zh: 自加元服，變態轉興，內外稍無以制。

translations.literal: From when he received the capping ceremony, his perverse conduct arose and turned; inside and outside gradually none could control him.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he received the capping ceremony his perverse conduct grew ever worse, and gradually none within or without the palace could control him.

sentences.zh: 三年秋冬間，便好出遊行，太妃每乘青篾車，隨相檢攝。

translations.literal: Between autumn and winter of the third year he took to outings; the imperial consort each time rode in a green bamboo-ribbed carriage to follow and check him.
translations.idiomatic: Between autumn and winter of the third year he took to going out on excursions; the imperial consort would each time ride in a green bamboo-ribbed carriage to follow and keep watch over him.

sentences.zh: 昱漸自放恣，太妃不復能禁。

translations.literal: Yu gradually let himself go unrestrained; the imperial consort could no longer restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gradually gave himself over to license, and the imperial consort could no longer restrain him.

sentences.zh: 單將左右，棄部伍，或十里、二十里，或入市里，或往營署，日暮乃歸。

translations.literal: He led only his attendants, abandoning formation — sometimes ten or twenty li, sometimes into market wards, sometimes to military camps — returning only at day's end.
translations.idiomatic: He led only his attendants and abandoned formation, going sometimes ten or twenty li, sometimes into the market wards, sometimes to military camps, and returning only at day's end.

sentences.zh: 四年春夏，此行彌數。

translations.literal: In spring and summer of the fourth year these outings grew ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer of the fourth year these outings became ever more frequent.

sentences.zh: 自京城剋定，意志轉驕，於是無日不出。

translations.literal: Once the capital had been secured, his will turned ever prouder, and from then on not a day passed without his going out.
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital had been secured his will grew ever prouder, and from then on there was not a day when he did not go out.

sentences.zh: 與左右人解僧智、張五兒恒相馳逐，夜出，開承明門，夕去晨反，晨出暮歸。

translations.literal: With his men Jie Sengzhi and Zhang Wu'er he constantly raced in chase — going out at night, opening Chenming Gate, leaving at evening and returning at dawn, or leaving at dawn and returning at evening.
translations.idiomatic: With his men Jie Sengzhi and Zhang Wu'er he constantly raced about: going out at night, opening Chenming Gate, leaving in the evening and returning at dawn, or leaving at dawn and returning in the evening.

sentences.zh: 從者並執鋋矛，行人男女，及犬馬牛驢，值無免者。

translations.literal: Those following all carried iron-shafted spears; men and women among travelers, and dogs, horses, cattle, and donkeys — none who met them escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Those who followed him all carried iron-shafted spears. Men and women on the road, and dogs, horses, cattle, and donkeys — none who encountered them escaped.

sentences.zh: 民間擾懼，晝日不敢開門，道上行人殆絕。

translations.literal: The people were disturbed and fearful; in broad daylight they dared not open their doors, and travelers on the roads were nearly extinct.
translations.idiomatic: The people were disturbed and afraid; in broad daylight they dared not open their doors, and travelers on the roads nearly disappeared.

sentences.zh: 常著小袴褶，未嘗服衣冠。

translations.literal: He constantly wore short jacket and trousers, never donning cap and gown.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly wore short jacket and trousers and never put on cap and gown.

sentences.zh: 或有忤意，輒加以虐刑。

translations.literal: If anyone displeased him, he at once inflicted cruel punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone displeased him, he at once inflicted cruel punishment.

sentences.zh: 有白棓數十枚，各有名號，鍼椎鑿鋸之徒，不離左右。

translations.literal: He had several dozen white clubs each with its own name; awls, mallets, chisels, saws and the like never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: He kept several dozen white clubs, each with its own name, and awls, mallets, chisels, saws, and the like never left his side.

sentences.zh: 嘗以鐵椎椎人陰破，左右人見之有斂眉者，昱大怒，令此人袒胛正立，以矛刺胛洞過。

translations.literal: Once he smashed a man's groin with an iron mallet; when an attendant seeing this knit his brows, Yu flew into rage and ordered the man stripped to the shoulders and made to stand straight while a spear was thrust through his shoulder blade and out the other side.
translations.idiomatic: Once he smashed a man's groin with an iron mallet. When an attendant who saw this knit his brows, Yu flew into a rage and ordered the man stripped to the shoulders and made to stand upright while a spear was thrust through his shoulder blade and out the other side.

sentences.zh: 於耀靈殿上養驢數十頭，所自乘馬，養於御牀側。

translations.literal: On the Hall of Glorious Spirit he kept several dozen donkeys; the horse he himself rode was stabled beside the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hall of Glorious Spirit he kept several dozen donkeys, and the horse he himself rode was stabled beside the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 先是民間訛言，謂太宗不男，陳太妃本李道兒妾，道路之言，或云道兒子也。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a popular rumor that Emperor Ming was not virile; the Chen imperial consort had originally been concubine to Li Dao'er, and street talk sometimes said Yu was Li's son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been a popular rumor that Emperor Ming was not virile. The Chen imperial consort had originally been a concubine of Li Dao'er, and street talk sometimes said that Yu was Li's son.

sentences.zh: 昱每出入去來，常自稱劉統，或自號李將軍。

translations.literal: Whenever Yu went out or came in he often called himself Liu Tong, or styled himself General Li.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yu went out or came in he often called himself Liu Tong or styled himself General Li.

sentences.zh: 與右衞翼輦營女子私通，每從之遊，持數千錢，供酒肉之費。

translations.literal: He privately had relations with women of the Right Guard Palanquin Camp and would go roaming with them, carrying several thousand in cash for wine and meat expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly consorted with women of the Right Guard Palanquin Camp and would go roaming with them, carrying several thousand cash for wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫腹心人張羊為佃夫所委信。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang, a man in Ruan Tianfu's inner confidence, was entrusted by Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang, a man in whom Ruan Tianfu placed his inner trust, was entrusted by Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 佃夫敗，叛走，後捕得，昱自於承明門以車轢殺之。

translations.literal: When Tianfu fell, Yang fled in rebellion; later captured, Yu personally ran him over with a cart at Chenming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianfu fell, Yang fled in rebellion. Later, when he was captured, Yu personally ran him over with a cart at Chenming Gate.

sentences.zh: 杜延載、沈勃、杜幼文、孫超，皆躬運矛鋋，手自臠割。

translations.literal: Du Yanzai, Shen Bo, Du Youwen, and Sun Chao — he all personally wielded spear and blade and cut them apart with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: For Du Yanzai, Shen Bo, Du Youwen, and Sun Chao he personally wielded spear and blade and cut them apart with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 執幼文兄叔文於玄武湖北，昱馳馬執矟，自往刺之。

translations.literal: He seized Youwen's elder brother Shuwen north of Xuanyuan Lake; Yu spurred his horse, grasped his long spear, and went himself to stab him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Youwen's elder brother Shuwen north of Xuanyuan Lake. Yu spurred his horse, grasped his long spear, and went himself to stab him.

sentences.zh: 制露車一乘，其上施篷，乘以出入，從者不過數十人。

translations.literal: He devised an open carriage with an awning mounted on it, riding it in and out with followers numbering no more than several tens.
translations.idiomatic: He devised an open carriage with an awning on it and used it for his comings and goings, with no more than several tens of followers.

sentences.zh: 羽儀追之恒不及；

translations.literal: The ceremonial guard chasing him could never catch up;
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial guard that pursued him could never catch up;

sentences.zh: 又各慮禍，亦不敢追尋，唯整部伍，別在一處瞻望而已。

translations.literal: and each feared calamity, so none dared pursue — they only kept the formation arrayed apart in one place to watch from afar.
translations.idiomatic: and each feared disaster, so none dared pursue him. They only kept their formation in one place apart and watched from afar.

sentences.zh: 凡諸鄙事，過目則能，鍛鍊金銀，裁衣作帽，莫不精絕。

translations.literal: Of all vulgar crafts whatever passed before his eyes he could do — forging and refining gold and silver, cutting cloth and making hats — none not done to ultimate excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Of all vulgar crafts, whatever passed before his eyes he could do — forging and refining gold and silver, cutting cloth and making hats — and none but was done to consummate skill.

sentences.zh: 未嘗吹篪，執管便韻。

translations.literal: He had never studied the chi pipe, yet taking a tube he at once found the modes.
translations.idiomatic: He had never studied the chi pipe, yet when he took up a tube he at once found the proper tones.

sentences.zh: 天性好殺，以此為歡，一日無事，輒慘慘不樂。

translations.literal: By nature he loved killing; this was his delight — a day without business and he was gloomy and joyless.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved killing and took his delight in it. A day without such business left him gloomy and joyless.

sentences.zh: 內外百司，人不自保，殿省憂遑，夕不及旦。

translations.literal: Inside and outside, the hundred offices — men could not preserve themselves; palace departments were anxious and unsettled, evening not reaching dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the palace, in the hundred offices, no one could feel safe. The palace departments lived in dread, and evening did not seem to reach dawn.

sentences.zh: 齊王順天人之心，潛圖廢立，與直閤將軍王敬則謀之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi conformed to the hearts of heaven and men and secretly plotted deposition and enthronement, taking counsel with Colonel Director Wang Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi followed the hearts of heaven and men and secretly plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone another, taking counsel with Colonel Director Wang Jingze.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，昱乘露車，從二百許人，無復鹵簿羽儀，往青園尼寺，晚至新安寺就曇度道人飲酒。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode his open carriage with some two hundred followers, no longer with imperial guard or feathered insignia, going to Qingyuan Nunnery and in the evening arriving at Xin'an Temple to drink with the Daoist adept Tandu.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode his open carriage with some two hundred men, no longer with imperial guard or feathered insignia. He went to Qingyuan Nunnery and in the evening arrived at Xin'an Temple to drink with the Daoist adept Tandu.

sentences.zh: 醉，夕扶還於仁壽殿東阿氈幄中臥。

translations.literal: Drunk, at evening he was helped back to lie in the felt tent east of the Hall of Human Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he was helped back in the evening to lie in the felt tent east of the Hall of Human Longevity.

sentences.zh: 時昱出入無恒，省內諸閤，夜皆不閉。

translations.literal: At that time Yu's comings and goings were without regularity; within the palace the various pavilions at night were all left unclosed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu's comings and goings had no fixed pattern, and within the palace the various pavilions were left unclosed at night.

sentences.zh: 且羣下畏相逢值，無敢出者。

translations.literal: Moreover the court feared meeting him and none dared go out.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the courtiers feared encountering him, and none dared go out.

sentences.zh: 宿衞並逃避，內外無相禁攝。

translations.literal: Night guards all fled, and inside and outside none restrained or seized one another.
translations.idiomatic: The night guards all fled, and inside and outside the palace none restrained or seized anyone.

sentences.zh: 王敬則先結昱左右楊玉夫、楊萬年、呂欣之、湯成之、陳奉伯、張石留、羅僧智、鍾千載、嚴道福、雷道賜、戴昭祖、許啟、戚元寶、盛道泰、鍾千秋、王天寶、公上延孫、俞成、錢道寶、馬敬之、陳寶直、吳璩之、劉印魯、唐天寶、俞孫等二十五人，謀共取昱。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze had first won over Yu's attendants Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, Lü Xinzi, Tang Chengzhi, Chen Fengbo, Zhang Shiliu, Luo Sengzhi, Zhong Qianzai, Yan Daofu, Lei Daoci, Dai Zhaozu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuanbao, Sheng Daotai, Zhong Qianqiu, Wang Tianbao, Gong Shangyansun, Yu Cheng, Qian Daobao, Ma Jingzhi, Chen Baozhi, Wu Qunzhi, Liu Yinlu, Tang Tianbao, Yu Sun, and twenty-five others in all, and they plotted together to seize Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze had first won over Yu's attendants Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, Lü Xinzi, Tang Chengzhi, Chen Fengbo, Zhang Shiliu, Luo Sengzhi, Zhong Qianzai, Yan Daofu, Lei Daoci, Dai Zhaozu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuanbao, Sheng Daotai, Zhong Qianqiu, Wang Tianbao, Gong Shangyansun, Yu Cheng, Qian Daobao, Ma Jingzhi, Chen Baozhi, Wu Qunzhi, Liu Yinlu, Tang Tianbao, Yu Sun, and twenty-five others in all, and they plotted together to seize Yu.

sentences.zh: 其夕，敬則出外，玉夫見昱醉熟無所知，乃與萬年同入氈幄內，以昱防身刀斬之。

translations.literal: That evening Jingze went out; Yufu, seeing Yu drunk and insensible, entered the felt tent with Wannian and struck him with Yu's own guard sword.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Jingze went out. Yufu, seeing that Yu was drunk and insensible, entered the felt tent with Wannian and struck him with Yu's own guard sword.

sentences.zh: 奉伯提昱首，依常行法，稱敕開承明門出，以首與敬則，馳至領軍府，以首呈齊王。

translations.literal: Fengbo took Yu's head, and following the usual procedure claimed an imperial command to open Chenming Gate and go out; he gave the head to Jingze, who rode to the headquarters of the Army Director and presented it to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo took Yu's head and, following the usual procedure, claimed an imperial command to open Chenming Gate and go out. He gave the head to Jingze, who rode to the headquarters of the Army Director and presented it to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 王乃戎服，率左右數十人，稱行還，開承明門入。

translations.literal: The prince donned military garb, led several tens of his men, claiming to be returning on circuit, opened Chenming Gate and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The prince put on military garb, led several tens of his men, claimed to be returning on circuit, opened Chenming Gate, and entered.

sentences.zh: 昱他夕每開門，門者震懾不敢視，至是弗之疑。

translations.literal: On other nights when Yu opened the gate the gatekeepers were awed and did not dare look; this time they suspected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: On other nights when Yu opened the gate the gatekeepers were awed and did not dare look up; this time they suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 齊王既入，曉，乃奉太后令奉迎安成王。

translations.literal: Once the prince had entered, at dawn he then followed the empress dowager's order to welcome the Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once the prince had entered, at dawn he then carried out the empress dowager's order to welcome the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：喪國亡家之主，雖適末同途，發軫或異也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Rulers who lose their states and destroy their families, though at the end their paths are the same, may differ in how they set out.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Rulers who lose their states and destroy their families, though at the end their paths are the same, may differ in how they set out.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝卑遊褻幸，皆龍駕帝飾，傳警清路；

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor's base roaming and illicit favors all used the dragon carriage and imperial adornment, with cleared roads and posted guards;
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor's base roaming and illicit favors all used the dragon carriage and imperial adornment, with cleared roads and posted guards;

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王則藏璽懷紱，魚服忘反，危冠短服，匹馬孤征。

translations.literal: the King of Cangwu hid the seal and wore the ribbon, fish-skin dress forgetting return, tall crown and short coat, lone horse on a solitary journey.
translations.idiomatic: the King of Cangwu hid the seal and wore the ribbon, dressed in fish-skin garb and forgetting to return, tall crown and short coat, a lone horse on a solitary journey.

sentences.zh: 至於殞身覆祚，其理若一。

translations.literal: As for body destroyed and fortune overturned, the principle is as one.
translations.idiomatic: As for the destruction of their persons and the overturning of their fortunes, the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 姬、夏之隆，質文異尚，亡國之道，其亦然乎。

translations.literal: At the greatness of Ji and Xia, substance and pattern differed in esteem; the way of losing a state — is it likewise?
translations.idiomatic: At the greatness of Ji and Xia, substance and ornament differed in what was honored; is the way of losing a state likewise?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛卯 下有辛未。

translations.literal: Below "In the tenth month of winter, on xinmao day" the editions have "on xinwei day."
translations.idiomatic: Below "In the tenth month of winter, on xinmao day" the editions have "on xinwei day."

sentences.zh: 按是月庚戌朔，二十二日辛未，無辛卯。

translations.literal: According to this, the first day of the month was gengxu; the twenty-second day was xinwei — there was no xinmao.
translations.idiomatic: According to this, the first day of the month was gengxu; the twenty-second day was xinwei — there was no xinmao.

sentences.zh: 以越州刺史陳伯紹為交州刺史 張森楷校勘記云：「按明帝紀，泰始五年，伯紹為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Bozhao, Inspector of Yue Province, was made Inspector of Jiao Province — Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "According to the Annals of Emperor Ming, in the fifth year of Taishi, Bozhao was Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhao, Inspector of Yue Province, was made Inspector of Jiao Province — Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "According to the Annals of Emperor Ming, in the fifth year of Taishi, Bozhao was Inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 七年，置越州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Yue Province was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Yue Province was established.

sentences.zh: 南齊書州郡志云，元徽二年，陳伯紹為越州刺史，當即指此。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies in the Book of Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui, Chen Bozhao was Inspector of Yue Province — this must refer to the present passage.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies in the Book of Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui Chen Bozhao was Inspector of Yue Province — this must refer to the present passage.

sentences.zh: 此當是以交州刺史陳伯紹為越州刺史，刻譌互倒。」

translations.literal: Here it should be that Chen Bozhao, Inspector of Jiao Province, was made Inspector of Yue Province — the characters were transposed in carving."
translations.idiomatic: Here it should read that Chen Bozhao, Inspector of Jiao Province, was made Inspector of Yue Province — the characters were transposed in carving."

sentences.zh: 五月壬午「壬午」各本並作「壬子」，據南史、建康實錄、通鑑改。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, "renwu" — all editions read "renzi"; corrected according to the History of Southern Dynasties, the Veritable Records of Jiankang, and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, "renwu" — all editions read "renzi"; corrected according to the History of Southern Dynasties, the Veritable Records of Jiankang, and the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 按是月辛未朔，十三日壬午，無壬子。

translations.literal: According to this, the first day of the month was xinwei; the thirteenth day was renwu — there was no renzi.
translations.idiomatic: According to this, the first day of the month was xinwei; the thirteenth day was renwu — there was no renzi.

sentences.zh: 賊黨杜黑蠡丁文豪分軍向朱雀航「杜黑蠡」魏書作「杜黑騾」。

translations.literal: The rebel band under Du Heili and Ding Wenhao divided their forces toward Zhuque Ford — "Du Heili" in the Book of Wei is written "Du Heilü."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel band under Du Heili and Ding Wenhao divided their forces toward Zhuque Ford — "Du Heili" in the Book of Wei is written "Du Heilü."

sentences.zh: 甲午 各本並作「戊午」，據局本及南史、建康實錄改。

translations.literal: "jiawu" — all editions read "wuwu"; corrected according to the Bureau edition and the History of Southern Dynasties and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: "jiawu" — all editions read "wuwu"; corrected according to the Bureau edition, the History of Southern Dynasties, and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 是月辛未朔，二十四日甲午，無戊午。

translations.literal: That month the first day was xinwei; the twenty-fourth day was jiawu — there was no wuwu.
translations.idiomatic: That month the first day was xinwei; the twenty-fourth day was jiawu — there was no wuwu.

sentences.zh: 撫軍典籤茅恬開東府納賊「撫軍」南史作「車騎」，建康實錄作「護軍」。

translations.literal: Mao Tian, Registrar of the Army Who Pacifies the Rebels, opened the Eastern Palace to admit the rebels — "Army Who Pacifies the Rebels" in the History of Southern Dynasties is written "General of Chariots and Cavalry," and in the Veritable Records of Jiankang "General Who Protects the Army."
translations.idiomatic: Mao Tian, Registrar of the Army Who Pacifies the Rebels, opened the Eastern Palace to admit the rebels — "Army Who Pacifies the Rebels" in the History of Southern Dynasties is written "General of Chariots and Cavalry," and in the Veritable Records of Jiankang "General Who Protects the Army."

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍南徐州刺史建平王景素進號征北將軍 各本並脫「南」字，據景素傳補。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingping, Jingsu, General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Southern Xu Province, was advanced to General Who Campaigns North — all editions omit the character "Southern"; supplied according to Jingsu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pingping, Jingsu, General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Southern Xu Province, was promoted to General Who Campaigns North — all editions omit the character "Southern"; supplied according to Jingsu's biography.

sentences.zh: 穀人五斛 各本並脫「人」字，據元龜二０七補。

translations.literal: five hu of grain per person — all editions omit the character "person"; supplied according to the Yuan Gui, fascicle 207.
translations.idiomatic: five hu of grain per person — all editions omit the character "person"; supplied according to the Yuan Gui, fascicle 207.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子 按是月癸亥朔，無庚子，初三日庚午，庚子或是庚午之譌。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengzi day — according to this, the first day of the month was guihai; there was no gengzi day. The third day was gengwu; gengzi may be a corruption of gengwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengzi day — according to this, the first day of the month was guihai; there was no gengzi day. The third day was gengwu; gengzi may be a corruption of gengwu.

sentences.zh: 而國度弘費「弘」各本並作「引」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: yet state expenditures are vast — "vast" in all editions is written "drawn"; corrected according to the Yuan Gui, fascicle 471.
translations.idiomatic: yet state expenditures are vast — "vast" in all editions is written "drawn"; corrected according to the Yuan Gui, fascicle 471.

sentences.zh: 則氓隸齊歡「隸」各本並作「祇」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: then commoners and servants alike would rejoice — "commoners" in all editions is written "only"; corrected according to the Yuan Gui, fascicle 471.
translations.idiomatic: then commoners and servants alike would rejoice — "commoners" in all editions is written "only"; corrected according to the Yuan Gui, fascicle 471.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍全景文為南豫州刺史「驍騎」各本並作「驃騎」，據南齊書呂安國傳全景文附傳改。

translations.literal: Quan Jingwen, General of Valiant Cavalry, was made Inspector of Southern Yu Province — "Valiant Cavalry" in all editions is written "Agile Cavalry"; corrected according to the biography of Quan Jingwen appended to Lü Anguo's biography in the Book of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingwen, General of Valiant Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Southern Yu Province — "Valiant Cavalry" in all editions is written "Agile Cavalry"; corrected according to the biography of Quan Jingwen appended to Lü Anguo's biography in the Book of Southern Qi.
